cgst-r48.plainEnglish: **Rule 48 — manner of issuing an invoice; e-invoicing.** A registered person whose **aggregate turnover in any financial year from 2017-18 exceeds the notified limit (currently 5 crore)** must prepare the invoice by uploading the specified particulars (**FORM GST INV-01**) to the **Invoice Registration Portal (IRP)** and obtaining an **Invoice Reference Number (IRN)**. cgst-r56.plainEnglish:
**Rule 56 — records to be maintained.** Every registered person keeps a true and
correct account of:
- goods / services **imported or exported**, and supplies attracting **reverse
  charge**, with the relevant documents (invoices, bills of entry, delivery
  challans, credit / debit notes, receipt / payment / refund vouchers,
  e-way bills);
- a **stock register** — opening balance, receipts, supplies, goods lost /
  stolen / destroyed / written off / given as gifts / free samples, and closing
  balance (raw materials, finished goods, scrap, wastage);
- **advances** received / paid and adjustments;
- details of **suppliers and customers** (name and address), and the **address of
  the premises** where goods are stored (including goods in transit).
An **agent** additionally keeps authorisations, description / value / quantity of
goods received and supplied on behalf of each principal, and details of the
account furnished to each principal. A **works contractor**, and a person
**manufacturing** goods, keep further prescribed particulars.

cgst-r69.plainEnglish: **Rule 69 — [Omitted w.e.f. 01.10.2022].** Prescribed how a recipient's **claim of input tax credit in GSTR-2** was matched, invoice by invoice, against the supplier's GSTR-1 (and against the IGST paid at customs). It implemented **section 42**, which is itself now omitted. Matching today is done through **GSTR-2B**, Rule 36(4) and section 16(2)(aa)/(ba); supplier-vs-return mismatches are handled under Rules 88C / 88D (DRC-01B / DRC-01C).

cgst-r70.plainEnglish: **Rule 70 — [Omitted w.e.f. 01.10.2022].** Provided for the **final acceptance** of the input tax credit that had matched under Rule 69, and its communication to the recipient in FORM GST MIS-1. Part of the shelved section 42 matching scheme.

cgst-r71.plainEnglish: **Rule 71 — [Omitted w.e.f. 01.10.2022].** Set out how a **discrepancy** in a matched ITC claim (excess claim, duplication, supplier default) was communicated to both parties (MIS-1 / MIS-2) and, if not rectified, **added to the recipient's output tax liability** with interest. Superseded by the GSTR-2B / section 16(2)(aa) regime and Rules 88C-88D.

cgst-r72.plainEnglish: **Rule 72 — [Omitted w.e.f. 01.10.2022].** Dealt with **input tax credit claimed on the same invoice more than once** — the duplicate was communicated to the recipient and added back to output tax liability. Part of the shelved section 42 scheme.

cgst-r73.plainEnglish: **Rule 73 — [Omitted w.e.f. 01.10.2022].** The output-tax-liability mirror of Rule 69 — it matched a supplier's **claim of reduction in output tax liability** (on a credit note) against the recipient's corresponding reversal of ITC. Implemented **section 43**, now omitted.

cgst-r74.plainEnglish: **Rule 74 — [Omitted w.e.f. 01.10.2022].** Provided for **final acceptance** of a matched reduction in output tax liability and its communication. Part of the shelved section 43 scheme.

cgst-r75.plainEnglish: **Rule 75 — [Omitted w.e.f. 01.10.2022].** Communicated a **discrepancy** in a claimed reduction in output tax liability and, on non-rectification, **added it back to the supplier's output tax liability** with interest. Superseded by the current credit-note rules under section 34 read with section 15(3).

cgst-r76.plainEnglish: **Rule 76 — [Omitted w.e.f. 01.10.2022].** Dealt with a **reduction in output tax liability claimed more than once** on the same credit note. Part of the shelved section 43 scheme.

cgst-r77.plainEnglish: **Rule 77 — [Omitted w.e.f. 01.10.2022].** Allowed a **refund of the interest** a taxpayer had paid when an ITC claim or a liability-reduction claim was reversed under Rules 71 / 75 and later re-claimed after the discrepancy was resolved. Redundant once the matching scheme was withdrawn.

cgst-r78.plainEnglish: **Rule 78 — matching of TCS details.** The details of supplies furnished by an **e-commerce operator** in GSTR-8 are matched with the supplier's outward supplies in GSTR-1. A discrepancy is communicated to both; if not rectified, it is added to the supplier's output tax for the next month with interest.

cgst-r83.plainEnglish:
**Rule 83 — enrolment and functioning of a GST practitioner (GSTP).** Carries out section 48.
- **Who may enrol (83(1))**: a citizen of India, of sound mind, not insolvent or convicted, who is *either* a retired Commercial-Tax / CBIC officer of Group-B or above with ≥2 years' service; *or* was a sales-tax practitioner / tax-return preparer for ≥5 years under the earlier law; *or* holds a commerce / law / banking / business-administration degree (or CA / CS / CMA) from a recognised university; *or* passed a notified departmental exam.
- **How (83(1))**: apply in **FORM GST PCT-01** on the portal; on enquiry the officer enrols in **PCT-02** or rejects (83(2)).
- **Validity (83(3))**: enrolment is valid until cancelled. A practitioner from the earlier law enrolled on a provisional basis had to pass the exam within the notified period (the deadline was extended several times).
- **Cancellation (83(4))**: for misconduct, after a PCT-03 show-cause and an order in **PCT-04**.
- **What a GSTP can do (83(8))**: prepare/furnish GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, GSTR-4, GSTR-9; file refund and registration-amendment / cancellation applications; deposit into the cash ledger; appear as an authorised representative. Every act needs the client's confirmation — **PCT-05** is the authorisation, and the client can withdraw it any time.
- **Responsibility (per s.48(3) / 83(9))**: correctness of anything filed always stays with the registered person, not the GSTP.

complianceChecklist.item: Hold a current PCT-02 enrolment certificate
Obtain a signed PCT-05 authorisation from each client before acting
Have the client approve every return / statement on the portal before filing
Retain working papers — correctness of the filing rests with the client, not you

cgst-r83.practicalNotes: The client must approve each return/statement on the portal before it is filed — a GSTP filing does not become final on its own. Keep a signed PCT-05 on record for every client. A GSTP enrolled in one State is treated as enrolled across India (83(11)). ITC-04 and the annual return can be filed by a GSTP; the monthly GSTR-3B payment still needs the client's confirmation of the challan.
commonMistakes: Filing without a recorded PCT-05 authorisation
Assuming a GSTP-prepared return is filed without the client's confirmation
Treating the GSTP as liable for errors — the registered person remains responsible (s.48(3))

cgst-r86a.plainEnglish: **Rule 86A — blocking of the electronic credit ledger.** An officer (Assistant Commissioner or above) who has **reasons to believe** that ITC in the ledger has been **fraudulently availed or is ineligible** — e.g. from a non-existent supplier, without receipt of goods / services, from a supplier who has not paid tax, or without a valid invoice — may **disallow the debit** of an amount equal to such credit, for up to **one year** (auto-unblocked thereafter). Reasons must be recorded; a post-decisional hearing is required (per case law).

complianceChecklist.item: On a Rule 86A block, obtain the recorded reasons and file objections

Confirm auto-unblocking after one year

cgst-r86a.practicalNotes: Rule 86A is heavily litigated. Courts (Delhi, Gujarat, Karnataka, Telangana) have held: the power needs **independent, recorded 'reasons to believe'** (not borrowed satisfaction), it cannot block **more than the available balance** or create a negative balance, and a **hearing / reasons** must be given. Seek the reasons immediately and file objections; if blocked beyond a year, it must auto-lift.

faqs.q: My credit ledger has been blocked under Rule 86A. What can I do?
faqs.a: Demand the written reasons, file an objection / representation, and if the blocking is unreasoned, borrowed, or exceeds the balance, challenge it by writ. It cannot last beyond one year and cannot exceed the credit actually in the ledger.

commonMistakes: Not challenging an unreasoned or borrowed-satisfaction block

caseLaw.name: Best Crop Science Pvt Ltd v. Principal Commissioner, CGST Commissionerate, Meerut
caseLaw.citation: [2024] 167 taxmann.com 244 (Del), W.P.(C) No. 10980 of 2024 and connected petitions, decided 23-09-2024; Revenue SLP dismissed / judgment affirmed by the Supreme Court on 17-07-2025
caseLaw.facts: Batch challenge to Rule 86A blocking orders, including 'negative blocking' beyond the available balance.
caseLaw.issue: Scope of Rule 86A — can it block more than the credit available, and what reasoning is required.
caseLaw.held: Rule 86A only allows disallowing debit of ITC **available** in the electronic credit ledger up to the amount believed to be fraudulently availed / ineligible; it cannot create or increase a negative balance or reach ITC yet to be credited. 'Reasons to believe' must be based on cogent material, be the officer's own, and be recorded; a block lapses automatically after one year.
caseLaw.effect: Leading authority against 'negative blocking' and unreasoned Rule 86A orders — reinforced by the Supreme Court's dismissal of the Revenue's challenge on 17-07-2025.

instructions.ref: Guidelines for disallowing debit of the electronic credit ledger under Rule 86A
instructions.gist: The power is to be exercised by an officer not below Assistant Commissioner, on his own 'reasons to believe' (not borrowed), recorded in writing, proportionate to the suspected ineligible credit, only against credit available in the ledger, and reviewed / unblocked once the reasons cease or after one year.

cgst-r86b.plainEnglish:
**Rule 86B — 1% mandatory cash payment.** A registered person whose **taxable turnover in a month exceeds 50 lakh** (excluding exempt and zero-rated) may **not** use the electronic credit ledger to discharge **more than 99%** of the output tax for that month — i.e. at least **1% must be paid in cash**. 

**Exceptions** (Rule 86B does not apply): the person / proprietor / karta / MD / partners have paid income-tax over 1 lakh in each of the last two years; a refund over 1 lakh received (zero-rated / inverted); cumulative cash payment already over 1% of cumulative output tax in the year; a Government department, PSU, local authority or statutory body.

complianceChecklist.item: Test Rule 86B every month against the 50-lakh taxable-turnover trigger
If an exception applies, keep the proof (ITR / refund / cumulative-cash working)
Pay at least 1% of output tax in cash where 86B applies

cgst-r88b.plainEnglish:
**Rule 88B — manner of calculating interest.** 
- **Late-filed return**: interest under section 50(1) is on the tax paid by **debiting the cash ledger**, for the period from the due date to the date of payment.
- **Other cases** (e.g. a demand): interest on the **total tax** unpaid, from the due date.
- **Wrongly availed and utilised ITC** (section 50(3)): interest only where the credit is **utilised**, from the date of utilisation to the date of reversal / payment; ITC is 'utilised' to the extent the credit-ledger balance falls below the wrong-ITC amount.

complianceChecklist.item: Compute late-return interest on the cash component only
For wrong ITC, test whether it was utilised before computing interest

cgst-r89.plainEnglish:
**Rule 89 — application for refund and the formulae.**
- **89(4)** zero-rated supply of goods / services **without payment** (LUT): **Refund = (Turnover of zero-rated supplies × Net ITC) ÷ Adjusted Total Turnover**. 'Turnover of zero-rated supply of goods' is capped at **1.5× the value of like domestic supplies**. 'Net ITC' = ITC availed on inputs and input services in the period.
- **89(5)** **inverted duty structure**: **Refund = {(Turnover of inverted-rated supply × Net ITC ÷ Adjusted Total Turnover) − tax payable on such inverted-rated supply × (Net ITC ÷ ITC availed on inputs and input services)}**. 'Net ITC' here is ITC on **inputs (goods) only** (upheld in *VKC Footsteps*; the second limb was added in 2022 for partial relief).
- Requires a statement of invoices, a declaration, and (where unjust enrichment applies) a CA certificate above 2 lakh.

complianceChecklist.item: Use the correct Rule 89(4) / 89(5) formula and 'Net ITC' definition
Exclude capital-goods ITC from 'Net ITC'
Apply the 1.5× cap on zero-rated goods turnover
Attach the invoice statement and, where needed, the CA certificate

caseLaw.name: Union of India v. VKC Footsteps India Pvt Ltd
caseLaw.citation: (2022) 2 SCC 603 / 2021 (52) GSTL 513 (SC) / [2021] 130 taxmann.com 193 (SC), Civil Appeal No. 4810 of 2021 and connected matters, decided 13-09-2021
caseLaw.facts: Challenge to Rule 89(5), which restricts the inverted-duty refund formula's 'Net ITC' to ITC on inputs (goods), excluding input services.
caseLaw.issue: Whether Rule 89(5) is ultra vires section 54(3) for excluding input-service ITC.
caseLaw.held: Rule 89(5) is valid and consistent with section 54(3)(ii) — the refund of unutilised ITC in an inverted structure is confined to ITC on inputs (goods). The Court, however, noted the anomalies in the formula and asked the GST Council to reconsider it (the formula's second limb was then added by Notification 14/2022-CT).
caseLaw.effect: Input-service ITC accumulated under an inverted structure is not refundable. The post-2022 formula gives partial relief but still excludes standalone input-service credit.

caseLaw.name: Amit Cotton Industries v. Principal Commissioner of Customs
caseLaw.citation: Gujarat High Court, R/Special Civil Application No. 20126 of 2018, decided 27-06-2019 (J.B. Pardiwala & A.C. Rao, JJ.); reported at 2019 (29) GSTL 200 (Guj) / [2019] 107 taxmann.com 167 (Gujarat)
caseLaw.facts: A cotton ginning mill exported cotton bales to Bangladesh in July 2017 on payment of IGST (about 19.05 lakh over three shipping bills) and also claimed duty drawback at the higher composite rate. Customs withheld the IGST-paid export refund, relying on the declaration required for higher drawback and on CBIC Circular 37/2018-Customs (9-10-2018), under which an exporter who claims the higher drawback rate is treated as having relinquished the IGST-refund claim. The exporter then repaid the differential drawback with interest and pressed for the refund; Customs still declined, saying the process is fully system-driven with no way to handle such a claim.
caseLaw.issue: Whether an IGST-paid export refund can be withheld merely because the exporter initially claimed drawback at the higher rate, relying on CBIC Circular 37/2018-Customs, when neither ground for withholding under Rule 96(4) of the CGST Rules is present.
caseLaw.held: The refund could not be withheld. Rule 96 creates a deeming fiction that the shipping bill is the refund application, and Rule 96(4) makes it 'abundantly clear' that a refund can be withheld only in the two situations in sub-clauses (a) and (b) — a withholding request from the jurisdictional Commissioner under section 54(10)/(11), or a Customs finding that the goods were exported in violation of the Customs Act — and the department fairly conceded neither applied. Circular 37/2018-Customs 'cannot be said to have any legal force' and 'cannot run contrary to the statutory rules, more particularly, Rule 96'; a circular contrary to statute 'has really no existence in law' (following Ratan Melting & Wire Industries and J.K. Lakshmi Cement, SC). The court also noted the circular post-dates the export (9-10-2018 vs 27-7-2017) and deals with drawback, not the IGST refund. 'Rule 96 of the Rules, 2017, is very clear.'
caseLaw.effect: The writ was allowed and Customs directed to sanction the IGST refund with 7% simple interest from the date of the shipping bills to actual refund. Widely followed by High Courts for the proposition that Rule 96(4) is an exhaustive list of the grounds to withhold an IGST-paid export refund and a circular cannot add to it. Separately, Rule 96(10) (a different bar, on concessional duty-free imports) was omitted with effect from 8 October 2024.

cgst-r96a.plainEnglish: **Rule 96A — export without payment of IGST (LUT / bond).** A registered person exporting under **LUT / bond (RFD-11)** must pay the IGST due **with interest** if: (a) **goods** are not exported within **3 months** of the invoice (or as extended); or (b) **payment for services** is not received in convertible forex within **1 year** of the invoice (or as extended). On subsequent export / realisation, the amount paid can be **refunded**.

complianceChecklist.item: File the LUT (RFD-11) at the start of each year
Export goods within 3 months of the invoice; realise service forex within 1 year
Seek an extension before the deadline; pay IGST + interest if it lapses, then claim refund on realisation

cgst-r138.plainEnglish:
**Rule 138 — the e-way bill.** Required before movement of goods of **consignment value exceeding 50,000** (with / without a supply, including job work, sales return and stock transfer). 
- **Part A** — invoice / value / HSN / transport document; **Part B** — vehicle number.
- **Validity** — **1 day per 200 km** (part thereof); for over-dimensional cargo, 1 day per 20 km. Extendable within **8 hours** before / after expiry.
- Part-B is not required for the first / last leg up to **50 km** within the State.
- An e-way bill is **mandatory regardless of value** for inter-State job-work movement and for movement of handicraft goods by an unregistered person.
- **Rule 138E** — a taxpayer who has not filed returns for **2 consecutive periods** (or a Rule 86B / suspended taxpayer) **cannot generate** e-way bills.

complianceChecklist.item: Generate an e-way bill for every movement above 50,000 and fill Part B
Auto-populate Part A from the e-invoice
Extend the e-way bill before expiry if transit is delayed
Keep returns filed so Rule 138E does not block e-way bills

faqs.q: Consignment value — is it inclusive of GST?
faqs.a: Yes. 'Consignment value' for the 50,000 threshold is the invoice value **including** tax, but **excluding** the value of exempt goods carried in the same conveyance.

faqs.q: Can I generate an e-way bill if I haven't filed returns?
faqs.a: No. Rule 138E blocks e-way bill generation (as consignor or consignee) for a taxpayer who has not filed returns for two consecutive tax periods, or who is suspended / Rule 86B restricted.

Voluntary / SCN-stage payment is in **DRC-03**; on acceptance, the officer issues **DRC-04** (acknowledgment) or **DRC-05** (conclusion). The order is accompanied by a **summary in DRC-07**; rectification / withdrawal in **DRC-08**. A **DRC-03A** mechanism now lets a DRC-03 payment be adjusted against a confirmed demand order.

complianceChecklist.item: Reconcile every DRC-01 / DRC-07 summary to the underlying SCN / order
Use DRC-03 for payments and DRC-03A to map them to a confirmed demand
Get a DRC-05 conclusion on record where the matter is closed by payment

cgst-r142.practicalNotes: Always check that a DRC-01/07 **summary** matches the detailed SCN / order — a demand raised only through a summary, without a proper SCN, is bad in law. Use **DRC-03A** to link an earlier DRC-03 payment to the demand order so it is not treated as unpaid.

cgst-r159.plainEnglish: **Rule 159 — provisional attachment of property.** The Commissioner's order under **section 83** is in **DRC-22**; a copy is sent to the relevant authority (bank / sub-registrar). cgst-r161.plainEnglish: **Rule 161 — continuation of recovery proceedings.** Where a demand is **increased or reduced** in appeal / revision, an **intimation (DRC-25)** of the revised amount is served, and recovery continues for the modified amount without a fresh notice for the part already covered.

cgst-r162.plainEnglish: **Rule 162 — compounding of offences.** Application in **CPD-01** to the Commissioner; a report is called from the officer; on being satisfied, the Commissioner passes an order in **CPD-02** specifying the **compounding amount** (25%–100% of the tax, within the floor and ceiling) to be paid within 30 days; on payment, the compounding is allowed and any prosecution is discharged; the order can be withdrawn if it was obtained by fraud / suppression.

complianceChecklist.item: File CPD-01; pay the compounding amount within 30 days of the CPD-02 order

cgst-r164.plainEnglish: **Rule 164 — procedure for the section 128A waiver (interest and penalty for FY 2017-18 to 2019-20).** The taxpayer files **SPL-01** (where only an SCN / statement is pending) or **SPL-02** (where an order has been passed), after **paying the full tax** by the notified date. The officer issues **SPL-05** (order concluding the proceedings) or **SPL-07** (rejection, appealable). Any appeal / writ on the same issue must be **withdrawn**. Amounts already paid towards interest / penalty are **not refunded**.

Pay the full tax by the notified date
File SPL-01 / SPL-02 within the window

igst-r1.plainEnglish: **Rule 1 of the IGST Rules — short title and commencement.** The IGST Rules, 2017 came into force on **22 June 2017**.

igst-r2.plainEnglish: **Rule 2 of the IGST Rules — application of the CGST Rules.** The **CGST Rules, 2017 apply** to integrated tax, so far as may be, as they apply to central tax (section 20 of the IGST Act). So there is a single set of procedural rules — registration, returns, ITC, refunds, e-way bill, demands — and the IGST Rules themselves add only the few special valuation / apportionment rules below.

igst-r3.plainEnglish: **Rule 3 — place of supply of advertisement services to the Government.** For advertisement services to the Central / State Government, a statutory body or a local authority that are supplied in more than one State (section 12(14)), the **proportion of value attributable to each State / UT** is worked out on the bases in the rule — for **newspapers / publications**, the edition-wise circulation; for **pamphlets / leaflets / diaries / calendars / T-shirts**, the quantity distributed in each State; for **hoardings** (other than trains), the location; for **trains**, the length of the railway track in each State; for **buses**, the route; for **the internet**, the number of internet subscribers; for **radio / TV**, the State of the broadcasting station / channel viewership; for **cinemas**, the location of the hall.

keyConcepts.note: Defined term — tap in the text to see the definition.
Defined term — tap in the text to see the definition.

igst-r4.plainEnglish: **Rule 4 — supply of services attributable to different States under section 12(3), (4), (5), (6) and (7)** where the immovable property / event / boat / vessel is located in **more than one State** and there is no contract specifying the split — the value is apportioned in the **ratio of the number of nights stayed / the area / the number of days / a reasonable basis** as set out for each category (e.g. hotel rooms in different States → nights in each; a training programme across States → participant-days; an event in multiple States → time and effort).

keyConcepts.note: Defined term — tap in the text to see the definition.

igst-r5.plainEnglish: **Rule 5 — services attributable to different States under section 13(3)(a)** (services on goods made physically available, or requiring the individual's physical presence) performed in **more than one country including India** — the value attributable to India is the proportion of **time spent / effort in India**, or a reasonable basis.

keyConcepts.note: Defined term — tap in the text to see the definition.

igst-r6.plainEnglish: **Rule 6 — leased circuits / telecommunication lines spanning multiple States (section 13(3)(b) read with 12(11))** — the value is apportioned in the **ratio of the number of points** (or the length of the circuit) in each State / UT.

keyConcepts.note: Defined term — tap in the text to see the definition.

igst-r7.plainEnglish: **Rule 7 — services under section 13(7)** (events / celebrations / conferences held in more than one State) where the recipient is outside India — apportion the value in the **ratio of the number of days** the event is held in each State / UT, or a reasonable basis, for the portion attributable to India.
